mutations.because: the identifier clause is defensive: no enabled Better Auth writer stores the email as identifier (magic-link stores a random token there), so only the planted v-1 row kills this. Replaced with `false`, v-1 survives and `expect(v1).toEqual([])` fails; the whole-database scan also finds the email on the identifier column.
command: eraseUser deletes verification rows whose identifier is the email

mutations.because: the value clause is the only half that reaches a magic-link row, whose identifier is a random token (v-2). With it replaced by `false` the row survives and `expect(v2).toEqual([])` fails; this is the row's own 'skip verification -> the scan finds the email' mutation, since v-2's value holds the target email and name.
command: eraseUser deletes magic-link verification rows whose value holds the email

mutations.because: the invitee delete is driven by INVITEE_MATCH; replacing it with `false` is the only statement that deletes an invitation addressed to the user, so inv-1 (Target@Example.COM) survives and the toEqual([]) read fails.
command: eraseUser deletes invitations sent to the email in any letter case

mutations.because: the sole-owner guard reads owners, so retargeting it at admins makes the REAL sole owner (LOCAL_OWNER, an owner not an admin) invisible and the erase proceeds. The refusal test then sees outcome `erased` instead of `sole-owner`, so the toEqual fails.
command: eraseUser refuses the only owner of an org and writes nothing

mutations.because: the memberCount recompute is a no-op under this mutant, so team-a stays at the seeded 2 instead of dropping to 1 and the receded count assertion fails.
command: eraseUser recounts memberCount for the teams the user left

mutations.because: without a transaction, steps 3-7 commit on the caller's connection before step 8 throws, so the failed-erase dump no longer equals the pre-call dump; the toEqual on the post-failure dump fails.
command: eraseUser rolls back every earlier step when the last step fails

mutations.before: update brief_version set actor = $2 where actor = $1
mutations.after: update brief_version set actor = $2 where actor = $1 and false
mutations.because: the actor rewrite is a no-op under this mutant, so the target's brief_version row keeps `u-target` instead of the token and the ordered actor read fails.
command: eraseUser replaces brief_version actor with the token and leaves another user untouched

mutations.because: the dry-run guard is removed, so a dry run (apply: false) falls through and performs the erase, answering `erased` instead of `planned`; the planned toEqual fails.
command: eraseUser dry run reports counts and changes nothing
